query: How should supported decision-making and proxy-consent be operationalized and documented in the field, and what pre-specified analytical adjustments will address proxy-reported responses?

response.query: How should supported decision-making and proxy-consent be operationalized and documented in the field, and what pre-specified analytical adjustments will address proxy-reported responses?
response.answer: Supported decision-making involves empowering individuals with assistance to make their own choices, while proxy-consent uses trusted individuals to make decisions when the person cannot. Documenting these processes requires clear records and consent. Analytical adjustments for proxy-reported responses should account for potential biases.

results.title: Reporting guideline for the early-stage clinical evaluation ...
results.content: Reporting guideline for the early-stage clinical evaluation of decision support systems driven by artificial intelligence: DECIDE-AI. Through consultation and consensus with a range of stakeholders, we developed a guideline comprising key items that should be reported in early-stage clinical studies of AI-based decision support systems in healthcare. Focusing on AI systems supporting, rather than replacing, human intelligence, DECIDE-AI aims to improve the reporting of studies describing the evaluation of AI-based decision support systems during their early, small-scale implementation in live clinical settings (that is, the supported decisions have an actual effect on patient care). An initial list of candidate items was developed based on expert opinion informed by (1) a systematic literature review focusing on the evaluation of AI-based diagnostic decision support systems3."); (2) an additional literature search about existing guidance for AI evaluation in clinical settings (search strategy available on the OSF44.")); (3) literature recommended by Steering Group members19."),22."),45."),46."),47."),48."),49."); and (4) institutional documents50."),51 Working Group.
